title: Sprint Sundown Rollout Notebook — Heuristic Experiments (2026-07)
body:
Purpose:
This notebook captures the operational checklist, experiment notes, and a compact rollout calendar for the "sprint sundown" release window. The goal: validate small-nighttime rollouts with conservative traffic ramping while trialing two alternative canary sampling heuristics (time-weighted vs. user-cohort). Use as the single source for preflight decisions and shift-handoff during the 72-hour window.

High-level goals:
- Keep customer-facing latency SLOs intact (p95 < 120ms)
- Limit blast radius via micro-cohorts and throttled ramp (max 10% traffic for first 6h)
- Evaluate heuristic A/B (HW) for sample-selection utility and impact on rollback sensitivity
- Capture post-release signal deltas in a short digest (24/72h notes)

Key dates (calendar):
- 2026-07-15 18:00 UTC — Dry-run in staging (full smoke + KB-cache priming)
- 2026-07-16 02:00 UTC — Night-window go/no-go meeting (on-call + SRE + Release lead)
- 2026-07-16 03:00 UTC — Canary start (10% traffic, cohort-based)
- 2026-07-16 09:00 UTC — Ramp to 40% if gates pass
- 2026-07-16 18:00 UTC — Ramp to 70% with throttles on non-critical routes
- 2026-07-17 02:00 UTC — Full release to 100% if stable
- 2026-07-18 18:00 UTC — Post-release 48h retro + metric digest

Preflight checklist (must be green before canary):
- [ ] Release artifact built and SHA verified (artifact: release-2026-07-sundown)
- [ ] Canary config committed (feature-flag: ff.sundown.heuristics) and PR merged (see linked PR)
- [ ] Staging dry-run completed, smoke failures = 0 for critical paths
- [ ] Traffic shaping rules deployed to the edge (max initial rate 10%)
- [ ] Observability dashboard pinned: latency, error-rate, request-volume, top-5 endpoints
- [ ] Regression prompt set (for model-serving) uploaded and baseline responses recorded
- [ ] Ops pager rotations assigned and acknowledged in #release-sundown channel
- [ ] Customer-facing comms drafted (brief note for the status page)

Staffing & rotations (night-window pattern):
- Release lead (primary): Aisha Patel — coordinates go/no-go and status posts
- SRE run lead: Miguel Santos — telemetry gating, infra remediation
- On-call infra: Priya Nair — handles host/GPU problems and autoscaler issues
- Monitoring & Logs: Benji Clarke — alert triage, data sampling
- Backup comms: rotation B (8-16 UTC) — Emma Zhou, Arun Iyer
Notes: pair the release lead with SRE run lead for first 6h; handoff doc must include last 15min snapshot and top 3 anomalies.

Telemetry gates and thresholds (automated checks + human review):
- Latency: p95 increase > 15% over baseline -> hold and investigate
- Error rate: 5xx > 0.5% absolute or > 3x baseline -> immediate rollback
- Throughput: drop > 20% while upstream 2xx remains -> suspect upstream throttling
- Quality regressions: prompt-eval A/B shows mean BLEU/score drop > 3 points -> manual review
- Queue depth on serving pods: sustained > 70% capacity -> throttle new canaries
Gating procedure: automated Slack alert + ephemeral ticket in JIRA-RELEASE-377; human on-call must ack within 5 minutes or we auto-throttle to previous variant.

Heuristic experiments (what we're testing):
- Experiment A: time-weighted sampling (prioritize recent sessions to capture peak patterns). Expected: faster signal arrival, but may over-index hot-paths.
- Experiment B: cohort sampling (randomized customer cohort by region + plan). Expected: better representativeness, slower convergence.
Design notes:
- Run A on region-us-west-2, run B on region-eu-central-1 simultaneously if capacity allows.
- Tag canary traces with experiment=A/B for filtering in dashboards.
- Capture per-experiment deltas and store a 24h snapshot (s3://release-artifacts/sundown/experiments/)

Rollback matrix (quick reference):
- Trigger: automated gate (error rate) -> Action: immediate rollback to previous stable model/variant, post-mortem flagged
- Trigger: latency p95 spike with matching increase in CPU/KV miss -> Action: throttle to 30% traffic and trigger infra triage
- Trigger: quality metric fail -> Action: pause rollout, human triage (DO NOT AUTO-ROLLBACK unless error-rate also tripped)
- Communication ladder: Release lead -> SRE -> Eng manager -> Customer success (if > 30% user impact)

Post-release notes template (for 24h and 72h digest):
- Summary: short paragraph of outcome and final traffic distribution
- Signals: p50/p95 latency, 5xx rates, traffic patterns by region
- Heuristic experiment summary: experiment A vs B key deltas (latency, errors, quality metric)
- Incidents: list of any triggered alerts and resolution timelines
- Action items: follow-ups with owners and due dates

Unresolved questions / TODOs (notes-to-self):
- Can we automate cohort assignment so that rollback can be targeted per-cohort? (JIRA ticket: ENG-1982)
- Need to finalize the prompt-eval runner for the regression set (Benji + Priya pairing)
- Confirm retention policy for experiment snapshots (how long keep 1:1 trace samples?)

Appendix: quick command snippets and links
- Canary toggle: ./release-tools toggle --flag ff.sundown.heuristics --on\n- Rollback: ./release-tools rollback --tag release-2026-07-sundown\n- Quick dashboards: https://metrics.redwood/s/release-sundown (pin this before start)\n- Slack preflight thread: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/CRELEASES/p1620......

End notes: keep this doc minimal and operational — move long-form retro into Confluence after 72h. If any automation gaps blocked an operator for >10 minutes during the window, log under "ops-automation-backlog" and tag with priority:high.

Signed-off-by: Aisha Patel (release lead)
